text:
Zero input embeddings do not skip GRU updates: recurrent terms, biases and gates still compute a new hidden state. Consequently, leading zero padding can change the state entering the first real event; masking loss afterward cannot undo this. This follows directly from [PyTorch’s GRU equations](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/generated/torch.nn.GRU.html).

Implementation implication: set `valid = sequence.ne(0)` and `lengths = valid.sum(1)`. Compact valid events chronologically into each row’s prefix, leaving right padding. Pack embeddings with `pack_padded_sequence(..., lengths.cpu(), batch_first=True, enforce_sorted=False)`, then run the unidirectional GRU. Packing retains the first `lengths[b]` positions, so passing left-padded inputs directly would retain padding and truncate real events. Handle empty rows separately; zero lengths cannot be packed. [Packing documentation](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/generated/torch.nn.utils.rnn.pack_padded_sequence.html).

For aligned next-item loss, unpack outputs and scatter each compact timestep back to its original valid sequence position. Keep positive/negative targets at their original positions and compute loss only where the input and target are valid. This preserves `log2feats(sequence)` as a left-aligned-to-original-input B×L×H interface. Select the greatest nonpadding index for readout—`L-1` for nonempty strictly left-padded histories—never `lengths-1` on the original layout. `lengths-1` is valid only within compacted outputs; packed GRU `h_n[-1]` also supplies the final state for a unidirectional model. Use identical compaction, scattering and readout in training, diagnostics and the embedded predictor. [Unpacking documentation](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.nn.utils.rnn.pad_packed_sequence.html).
